chunks: Ali, from his father, from Abdullah Bin Al Mugheira, from Amro Bin Abu Al Miqdam, (It has been narrated) raising it to the Prophet (peace be upon him and his family).
He said: 'In kindness there is increase and blessings; and whoever is deprived of kindness is deprived of goodness.'

key_terms.الرِّفْقِ: Kindness, gentleness, or ease in conduct
key_terms.الزِّيَادَةَ: Increase (often referring to sustenance or merit)

ai.seo_question: What is the spiritual and material benefit of practicing kindness (rifq) according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In al-Kafi, this hadith establishes الرفق (gentleness/kindness) as a fundamental spiritual mechanism that actively generates barakah (divine blessing) and sustenance, rather than merely being a moral virtue. It reflects the Shia emphasis on character refinement as a prerequisite for receiving comprehensive goodness, warning that the absence of gentleness leads to a holistic deprivation of benefit.
